title: Meningitis and Encephalitis: Empiric Coverage and Adjunctive Therapy
summary: Bacterial meningitis and encephalitis are medical emergencies. Initiate diagnostics and empiric antimicrobials immediately, with early dexamethasone in suspected pneumococcal meningitis. Add acyclovir when encephalitis is possible. Tailor therapy by age, immune status, exposure risks, and local resistance patterns. Early treatment within 1 hour reduces mortality and poor outcomes.
clinicalQuestion: What empiric antimicrobial regimens and adjunctive therapies should be initiated for suspected bacterial meningitis and encephalitis in adults, and what timing and outcome data support these choices?

heroStats.label: Time-to-antibiotics
heroStats.value: Initiate within 1 hour for suspected bacterial meningitis

heroStats.label: Outcome impact
heroStats.value: Each hour of delay ↑ unfavorable outcome by ~10–30%

heroStats.label: Steroid timing
heroStats.value: Give dexamethasone before or with first antibiotic dose

keyMoments.title: Immediate Actions
keyMoments.body: Stabilize ABCs, obtain blood cultures, start empiric antimicrobials and dexamethasone without delay when bacterial meningitis is suspected.

keyMoments.title: Imaging vs LP
keyMoments.body: Do not delay antibiotics for imaging. If LP is delayed for safety, treat first and LP as soon as feasible.

keyMoments.title: Add Acyclovir
keyMoments.body: If encephalitis is on the differential, add IV acyclovir pending HSV/VZV PCR.

keyMoments.title: Tight Glucose & Electrolytes
keyMoments.body: Monitor and correct hypoglycemia, hyponatremia (SIADH), and seizures early.

keyMoments.title: De-escalation
keyMoments.body: Refine therapy rapidly using CSF profile, Gram stain/PCR panels, culture, and clinical evolution.

sections.title: Initial Evaluation and Time-Critical Therapy
sections.blurb: Prompt antimicrobial therapy and steroids save lives; diagnostics should proceed in parallel.

steps.title: Stabilize and Draw Cultures
steps.body: Secure airway/breathing/circulation. Obtain two sets of blood cultures before antimicrobials when feasible, but do not delay treatment.

steps.title: Immediate Empiric Therapy
steps.body: Start antimicrobials within 1 hour for suspected bacterial meningitis; within 6 hours for suspected encephalitis if clinically safe. Each hour of delay increases unfavorable outcomes by approximately **10–30%** [6].

steps.title: Dexamethasone
steps.body: Administer dexamethasone before or with the first antibiotic dose in suspected pneumococcal meningitis to reduce mortality and neurologic sequelae; underused despite benefit [2], [3].

steps.title: Lumbar Puncture and Imaging
steps.body: Perform LP promptly unless signs of mass effect or herniation risk. If imaging is required, do not delay empiric therapy; treat first and image/LP as soon as possible [6].

steps.title: Add Acyclovir if Encephalitis Possible
steps.body: Start IV acyclovir empirically for suspected viral encephalitis while obtaining CSF HSV/VZV PCR; delay worsens outcomes [4], [6].

sections.title: Empiric Antimicrobial Coverage
sections.blurb: Regimens should cover likely pathogens by age, immune status, and local resistance. Adjust for allergies and renal function.

cards.title: Adults <50 years (Immunocompetent) – Suspected Bacterial Meningitis
items: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h (or cefotaxime 2 g IV q4–6h) + vancomycin dosed to trough/AUC for penicillin- and cephalosporin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae
Add dexamethasone 10 mg IV q6h x 4 days started before/with first antibiotic dose if pneumococcal disease suspected [2], [3].
If encephalitis cannot be excluded: add acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h [4], [6].

cards.title: Adults ≥50 years or with Alcoholism, Pregnancy, or Significant Comorbidity
items: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h (or cefotaxime) + vancomycin + ampicillin 2 g IV q4h for Listeria coverage.
Dexamethasone as above when pneumococcus suspected [2], [3].
Add acyclovir if encephalitis features present [4], [6].

cards.title: Immunocompromised (e.g., transplant, lymphoma, high-dose steroids)
items: Vancomycin + cefepime 2 g IV q8–12h (or meropenem 2 g IV q8h) + ampicillin for Listeria.
Consider TMP–SMX if sulfa-sensitive Listeria and penicillin allergy; consider anti-fungal/anti-TB based on risk and CSF profile [4], [6], [8].
Add acyclovir if encephalitis suspected.

cards.title: Severe Beta-lactam Allergy
items: Vancomycin + moxifloxacin 400 mg IV daily ± aztreonam 2 g IV q6–8h for Gram-negative coverage.
For Listeria: TMP–SMX 5 mg/kg (TMP) IV q6–8h.
Consult ID early for individualized regimens.

cards.title: Suspected Viral Encephalitis
items: Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h with aggressive IV hydration; adjust for renal function.
If tick exposure or seasonality suggests: add doxycycline 100 mg IV/PO q12h empirically for rickettsial illness pending tests.
Stop acyclovir if HSV/VZV PCR negative and alternative diagnosis established [4], [6].

cards.title: Diagnostics to Guide De-escalation
items: CSF opening pressure, cell count & differential, protein, CSF glucose with paired serum glucose, Gram stain/culture, multiplex PCR when available [6].
Blood cultures, serum/CSF PCR for HSV/VZV/enteroviruses; TB NAAT if suspected; HIV testing.
Neuroimaging if focal deficits, papilledema, immunocompromise, or seizures.

cards.title: Timing and Outcomes
items: Begin antibiotics within 1 hour of arrival for suspected bacterial meningitis; do not delay for imaging or LP [6].
Each hour of delay increases odds of poor outcome by roughly **10–30%** [6].
Steroids reduce mortality and neurologic sequelae in pneumococcal meningitis when given early; underutilized in practice [2], [3].

cards.title: Adjunctive Measures
items: Seizure management and prophylaxis for status epilepticus risk.
ICP management: head elevation, analgesia/sedation, hyperosmolar therapy as indicated; neurosurgical consult for obstructive hydrocephalus.
Electrolyte correction (SIADH-related hyponatremia), strict glucose control, DVT prophylaxis when safe.

cards.title: Tuberculous or Chronic Meningitis Considerations
items: If TB meningitis suspected, start empiric anti-TB therapy immediately (RIPE + adjunctive steroids) without waiting for culture/NAAT due to slow growth and high morbidity [8].
Obtain CSF AFB smear/culture, NAAT, and imaging for basal meningeal enhancement.
